*   **When to use:** High bitrates where view synthesis quality is acceptable (above the -0.05, -0.1, or -0.5 dB thresholds) and reconstructed image quality is prioritized over view synthesis [S1].

The claim states that the technique should be used at high bitrates where view synthesis quality is acceptable (specifically above the -0.05, -0.1, or -0.5 dB thresholds) and when reconstructed image quality is prioritized over view synthesis. Source [S1] explicitly supports this by stating: 'the residual coding is only applied at high bitrates where the quality of synthesised views is acceptable' and 'employed at bitrates higher than the bitrates in which the quality of the synthesised views reaches the values below the lossless quality at -0.05 dB, -0.1 dB and -0.5 dB.' Furthermore, the source notes that 'residual coding improves the compression performance of the codec but may deteriorate the view synthesis performance,' implying that its use involves a trade-off where reconstructed image quality is the primary benefit, potentially at the cost of view synthesis quality.

Residual coding is a technique that improves the compression performance (reconstructed image quality) of volumetric codecs by encoding the difference between the original image and the direct reconstructed image from the volume without quantization or coding [S1].

The claim states that residual coding improves compression performance (reconstructed image quality) by encoding the difference between the original image and the direct reconstructed image from the volume without quantization or coding. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

The method was proposed to address the limitations of standard volumetric coding where view synthesis quality might degrade at certain bitrates, while acknowledging that residuals do not help view synthesis [S1].

The claim states that the method was proposed to address limitations of standard volumetric coding where view synthesis quality might degrade at certain bitrates, while acknowledging that residuals do not help view synthesis. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Residual coding can be included in the coding technique to improve the quality of the reconstructed images; however, the residuals do not have any contribution to the quality of the view synthesis... residual coding improves the compression performance of the codec but may deteriorate the view synthesis performance at a particular bitrate.' It further explains that residuals are employed at bitrates higher than those where view synthesis quality drops below specific thresholds (e.g., -0.05 dB, -0.1 dB, -0.5 dB). This confirms that the method acknowledges the lack of benefit (and potential harm) of residuals to view synthesis and proposes a strategy to mitigate view synthesis degradation by selectively applying residuals only when view synthesis quality is acceptable.
